reason: The hypothesis applies the well-known mechanism of strengthening by ordered precipitates or local chemical order, demonstrated in Al-containing and refractory HEAs (P1, P2) and discussed generically for SRO (P5, P20, P28), to the specific, previously unstudied case of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state. It proposes a controlled thermal treatment to induce ordering in this alloy and predicts a strength-ductility trade-off, which is a direct transfer of a known concept to a new material system without integrating conflicting evidence or resolving a gap.
copied_elements: ordered phases (B2) impede dislocation motion, increasing strength and reducing ductility (P1, P2)
disordered solid solution has lower strength but higher ductility (P1, P2)
local chemical order/short-range order increases strength (P5, P20, P28)
thermal treatments can induce ordering/precipitation (general knowledge)
